story: Port MacKenzie rail extension wins final railroad board approval, with AIDEA's match back on an open board agenda and data center uses proposed at both ends of the line

repeat_reasons.reason: First response was incomplete. It returned sentence fragments with no subjects, such as 'gave final approval' with no actor or time reference and the $33 million sentence with no named payer. One targeted repeat fetched the full sentences.

claims.claim: The Alaska Railroad's board of directors gave final approval to the $311 million Port MacKenzie rail line in the week of November 16th.
claims.verbatim: This week, the board of directors for the state-owned railroad gave final approval for the $311 million rail line,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Article dated November 20th, so 'this week' means the week of November 16th. No ARRC board resolution was fetched, so treat the approval as reported by the Beacon. $249M grant plus $62M local share (C22) equals $311M, which is consistent. In June O'Leary put the cost at about $300 million (C29).

claims.claim: The 32-mile line will connect Port MacKenzie to the railroad's main line near Houston.
claims.verbatim: The 32-mile line will connect the port to the railroad’s main line near Houston
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Corroborated by Alaska Public Media, October 20th, which also gives 32 miles to the main line near Houston.

claims.claim: A $249 million federal grant will fund most of the rail extension.
claims.verbatim: A $249 million federal grant will fund most of the project
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Corroborated independently by Alaska Public Media (Bradner, October 20th) and by the Mat-Su Borough letter as reported November 17th.

claims.claim: AIDEA is expected to provide $33 million in matching funds to unlock the federal grant.
claims.verbatim: The Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority is expected to provide $33 million in matching funds
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: DISCREPANCY. The Beacon says $33 million. AIDEA's signed June 17th minutes authorize 'up to $34 million' (C24). Alaska Public Media says AIDEA covers 'about half' of the $62 million share, roughly $31 million (C23). Suggested wording is 'about $33 million, according to the Alaska Beacon', or 'up to $34 million' citing the board resolution. The match is also on the open agenda as 'Amended Second Resolution G26-07' (C33), so the final figure may change.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Borough will provide cash, land and gravel to fulfill the remainder of the required match.
claims.verbatim: will provide cash, land and gravel to fulfill the remainder of the required match.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The page spells it 'Matanuska-Sustina Borough', a typo in the source. Alaska Public Media (October 20th) says the borough covers its part 'with land and gravel'.

claims.claim: The Alaska Railroad will pay additional project costs from its savings.
claims.verbatim: the railroad will pay additional costs from savings
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: No dollar amount is given for the railroad's share.

claims.claim: Alaska Railroad CEO Bill O'Leary said the goal is to break ground this summer, depending on how fast the grantor agency moves.
claims.verbatim: Our goal is to really break ground this summer, but that is dependent upon a number of things
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: This is a stated goal and depends on conditions. The quote continues 'that are going to involve the grantor agency, and how fast they can move in getting the grant in place'. Phrase it as 'aims to' or 'could', never as a start date. If quoted, use the verbatim text exactly.

claims.claim: O'Leary said the railroad expects to know the grantor agency's stance on its timeline in about a month to six weeks.
claims.verbatim: month to six weeks about their stance on all that.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The full source sentence contains an em dash ('in the next — probably — month to six weeks'). If it is quoted, the house no-dash rule means paraphrasing. He said 'probably', so this is an estimate.

claims.claim: The rail spur was proposed as far back as 1992, before Port MacKenzie was built.
claims.verbatim: Proposed as far back as 1992, before Port MacKenzie was even built, the railroad spur didn’t begin moving forward
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Background history from a single outlet.

claims.claim: The project began moving forward in 2002, when proponents started clearing a 30-foot-wide right-of-way.
claims.verbatim: until 2002, when proponents started clearing a 30-foot-wide right-of-way.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Alaska Public Media puts state spending of $180 million at 2005 to 2017 (C21). That covers spending only and doesn't contradict a 2002 start of clearing.

claims.claim: The project was poised to move forward in 2007, but local opposition and a lack of funding stopped it.
claims.verbatim: The project was poised to move forward in 2007, but local opposition and a lack of funding stopped it again.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Alaska Public Media (October 20th) says work stopped in 2017 after state budget cuts. The two stoppages are different, 2007 and 2017. Don't merge them in copy.

claims.claim: The Alaska Legislature voted 58-1 in favor of a resolution backing the rail line.
claims.verbatim: the Alaska Legislature voted 58-1 in favor of a resolution backing the railroad line
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The response gave no resolution number or vote date. Don't attach a date or bill number. Single outlet, no primary fetched.

claims.claim: According to the Alaska Beacon, the developers of an antimony mine and of a coal-fired computing data center have announced construction projects at the port in anticipation of the rail line.
claims.verbatim: The developers of an antimony mine and a coal-fired computing data center have already announced construction projects at the port in anticipation of the rail line.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: SOFT SPOT. The Beacon doesn't name either developer. The fetch tool returned only fragments of this sentence. The full sentence matches the scout's quote and both fragments are on the page, but the joined text was never returned in one response, so confidence is lower. The likeliest candidate is Terra Energy Center Corporation, but Alaska Business (C49) says 'TECC isn't building a data center', so do NOT name Terra as the data center developer. Attribute to the Beacon ('according to the Alaska Beacon').

claims.claim: AIDEA voted to approve its share of the match on June 17th.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA voted to approve its share of the match on June 17
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Confirmed by the primary signed minutes (C24 to C28).

claims.claim: AIDEA's board was scheduled to discuss the rail match again at a meeting on Tuesday, November 24th.
claims.verbatim: Its board is scheduled to discuss that match again in a meeting scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 24.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The November 24th agenda PDF was not fetched. The primary November 19th agenda lists the item (C33), and the schedule page lists November 24th as the continued November 19th meeting (C31), now in recess to November 27th (C30). The outcome is unknown as of this run.

claims.claim: Gov.-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has asked AIDEA to pause spending actions until he takes office in early December.
claims.verbatim: Gov.-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has asked AIDEA to pause spending actions until he takes office
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Corroborated by Alaska Public Media, November 20th (C55), which gives December 7th as the date he takes office. That article doesn't mention Port MacKenzie, so the request is general and not aimed at the rail match.

claims.claim: O'Leary said he doesn't think the incoming governor will oppose the railroad project.
claims.verbatim: but O’Leary said he doesn’t think the incoming governor will oppose the railroad project.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: This is O'Leary's opinion and must stay attributed. The governor-elect's own position on the rail wasn't found. The page uses curly apostrophes.

claims.claim: The grant was paid for with money approved for a rail program under the bipartisan infrastructure law.
claims.verbatim: The grant was paid for with money approved for a rail program under the bipartisan infrastructure law
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The Beacon doesn't name CRISI. CRISI is named in the AIDEA June 17th minutes (C24, C27).

claims.claim: Sen. Dan Sullivan called the grant a major win for the Mat-Su Borough and the state.
claims.verbatim: This is a major win for the Mat-Su Borough and our entire state, and another important step
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: The page also says Sullivan 'lost re-election'. The quote continues 'toward unlocking Alaska’s extraordinary resource potential,'.

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski said good things happen in Alaska when infrastructure is funded at the federal level.
claims.verbatim: Good things happen in Alaska when we help fund infrastructure investments at the federal level.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), republished by Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Her earlier sentence contains an ellipsis in the source ('included the … program'). Use this sentence if quoting.

claims.claim: The state spent $180 million on the rail line between 2005 and 2017.
claims.verbatim: The state poured $180 million into the rail line between 2005 and 2017.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Tim Bradner, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Background, outside the news window. Commerce Commissioner Sande said 'approximately $180 million' in the June 17th minutes. The borough letter cites '$180 million spent on a rail bed' (C37).

claims.claim: The federal funding requires a $62 million local cost share.
claims.verbatim: The new funding requires a $62 million local cost share.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Tim Bradner, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Background. $249M plus $62M equals $311M, which matches C01. $62M is 20 percent of $311M, which fits the 20 percent match O'Leary described in June (C26).

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported in October that AIDEA agreed to cover about half of the $62 million local share.
claims.verbatim: has agreed to cover about half of that.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Tim Bradner, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: DISCREPANCY. Half of $62 million is about $31 million, against $33 million in the Beacon (C04) and 'up to $34 million' in the board resolution (C24). Use one sourced figure in copy and don't do the arithmetic for the reader. The response said the borough covers the rest 'with land and gravel', while the Beacon adds cash and railroad savings.

claims.claim: AIDEA's Amended Resolution G26-07 approved the use of up to $34 million from the AIDEA Revolving Fund as a partial match for the Alaska Railroad's CRISI grant.
claims.verbatim: approves the use of up to $34 million from the AIDEA Revolving Fund as the partial amount needed to match the competitive CRISI grant, if awarded to Alaska Railroad.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The source was the showrunner's text extraction at out/2026-11-25/aidea_june17_minutes.txt. This fact-checker didn't WebFetch the PDF. The minutes record the June 17th meeting and were signed August 26th, going by the folder and file name. The minutes say Executive Director Ruaro described the resolution. The figure is a ceiling ('up to'). Compare $33M in the Beacon. The open agenda item is now an 'Amended Second' version (C33).

claims.claim: AIDEA's board passed the Port MacKenzie resolution unanimously on a roll call on June 17th.
claims.verbatim: A roll call was taken, and the motion passed unanimously.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: Five members were present (Kendig, Sande, Fogle, Eledge, Haynes). Earls and Guy were absent. The motion recorded is 'to approve Resolution G26-07'. The text above it describes the amended resolution.

claims.claim: At the June 17th AIDEA meeting O'Leary said the grant required a 20 percent match of as much as $60 million.
claims.value: 20% match of as much as $60 million
claims.verbatim: the issue with the grant application is the required 20% match of as much as $60 million.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: This is the minute-taker's paraphrase, not a direct quote. Don't put it in quotation marks as O'Leary's words. The local share later became $62 million (C22).

claims.claim: O'Leary attended the June 17th AIDEA meeting in person and spoke in support of the Port MacKenzie rail extension item.
claims.verbatim: Bill O’Leary, President and Chief Executive Officer of Alaska Railroad, commented that he is pleased to be in attendance today and to support the Port MacKenzie rail extension agenda item.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: The meeting was held 'via Zoom', so 'in person' isn't supported. Drop it and say he attended and spoke during public comment. He also said the CRISI program 'closes next week'.

claims.claim: Ruaro told the board that AIDEA is not the only match provider, with the Mat-Su Borough and the railroad also contributing.
claims.value: Mat-Su Borough and the Railroad Corporation
claims.verbatim: AIDEA is not the only entity providing matching funds, and other entities include the Mat-Su Borough and the Railroad Corporation.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: Agrees with the Beacon's description of the borough and railroad contributions (C05, C06).

claims.claim: In June O'Leary put the project's outlay at approximately $300 million.
claims.verbatim: Mr. O’Leary noted that the outlay of the project is significant at approximately $300 million.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (signed board minutes)
claims.notes: This was the June estimate. The approved figure is $311 million (C01). Use $311M as the current number.

claims.claim: AIDEA's November 24th board meeting is in recess and will resume at 10 a.m. on Friday, November 27th.
claims.verbatim: The November 24, 2026 AIDEA Board Meeting is now in recess and will resume at 10:00 AM on Friday, November 27, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The page is live and has no date of its own. The date given is the run date, and the page was fetched on November 26th. The page says 'dates and times are subject to change'. The schedule also lists a separate 'Board Meeting' entry for November 27th.

claims.claim: AIDEA's schedule lists the November 24th meeting as a continuation of its November 19th board meeting.
claims.verbatim: Continued November 19, 2026, Board Meeting
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: Ties the November 19th agenda (C33) to the recessed meeting. 'value' holds the verbatim label because the claim turns on the continuation wording.

claims.claim: AIDEA's next regularly scheduled board meeting is Friday, December 4th.
claims.verbatim: Next regularly scheduled AIDEA Board Meeting: Friday, December 4, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (board agenda)
claims.notes: The schedule page also lists a 'Board Meeting' on Friday, December 04, 2026. The agenda puts it in the AHFC Board Room, 4300 Boniface Parkway, Anchorage. December 4th is three days before Kreiss-Tomkins takes office on December 7th.

claims.claim: The agenda for AIDEA's November 19th board meeting listed an Amended Second Resolution G26-07 on Port Mackenzie Infrastructure and Real Estate.
claims.verbatim: C Amended Second Resolution G26-07 Port Mackenzie Infrastructure and Real Estate
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (board agenda)
claims.notes: PRIMARY. WebFetch's text model saw only binary, but the tool saved the PDF from that same response and Read rendered it as readable text. No second fetch was made. The resolution's contents, including any new dollar figure, weren't fetched, so don't say what the amended second version changes. Item B on the same agenda is Resolution G26-05 Section 1002 Area Development Budget.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Borough's letter asking the state to reconsider the Houston land transfer was signed by Borough Manager Mike Brown and Mayor Edna DeVries.
claims.verbatim: The letter is signed by Borough Manager Mike Brown and Mayor Edna DeVries.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: The fetch tool may have paraphrased the verbatim line, but the signers are confirmed. The article says the letter was sent on 'Friday' and gives no calendar date. The scout's 'November 13th' is an inference and was killed. The letter itself wasn't fetched.

claims.claim: The borough letter says Point Mackenzie and portions of West Susitna offer more appropriate locations for the proposed uses.
claims.value: Point Mackenzie and portions of West Susitna
claims.verbatim: The Borough believes that Point Mackenzie and portions of West Susitna offer more appropriate locations for these uses.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Quoted from the letter in the article. The letter itself wasn't fetched.

claims.claim: The borough letter notes that $180 million has been spent on a rail bed slated to receive about $249 million in new federal funding.
claims.verbatim: $180 million spent on a rail bed that is slated to receive about $249 million in new federal funding for completion.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: This sentence ties the Houston land fight to the Port MacKenzie rail. Both figures match C21 and C03.

claims.claim: DNR approved a transfer of about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA, scaled back from an initial proposal of almost 20,000 acres.
claims.verbatim: reconsider a decision to transfer about 6,800 acres of land near Houston.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: The Alaska Current (C46) quotes DNR as reducing the transfer 'from 19,500 to approximately 6,800 acres'. Prefer 19,500 over 'almost 20,000'. The Mat-Su Sentinel DNR article gives 'about 11 square miles', about 7,040 acres, which is consistent.

claims.claim: DNR received more than 2,300 public comments on the no-cost transfer, almost all of them opposed.
claims.verbatim: received more than 2,300 public comments regarding the no-cost transfer, almost all of which opposed it.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Attributed to DNR in the article.

claims.claim: Anyone who commented on the transfer can request reconsideration by November 30th.
claims.verbatim: by Nov. 30.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Only the fragment came back verbatim. The rest of the sentence ('anyone who commented') is the tool's paraphrase. The DNR decision document wasn't fetched.

claims.claim: DNR has 30 days to respond to reconsideration requests.
claims.verbatim: DNR has 30 days to respond to those requests.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: The tool returned this as a bullet and may have paraphrased it. The fact is supported, but don't put the wording in quotation marks.

claims.claim: The Houston land transfer is the subject of a pending lawsuit.
claims.verbatim: The transfer is also the subject of a pending lawsuit.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: The plaintiff isn't named in the response.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins, who is sworn in on December 7th, has said he would completely reassess everything AIDEA is looking at.
claims.verbatim: completely reassess everything that AIDEA is looking at.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Quote the verbatim fragment only. The December 7th date is corroborated by Alaska Public Media, November 20th (C55).

claims.claim: An AIDEA proposal says the Houston land could be used for projects not yet identified, which could include an industrial hub or data centers.
claims.verbatim: projects that have not yet been identified, which could include an industrial hub or data centers,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel)
claims.notes: Data centers are a possible use only. Say 'could include'. Never call it a data center site as fact. Corroborated by the Alaska Current (C44, C45).

claims.claim: In July AIDEA said the Houston land could be used for a logistics hub, advanced manufacturing and scalable data centers.
claims.verbatim: could be used for a logistics hub, advanced manufacturing and "scalable data centers," but those plans were not certain.
claims.source_outlet: The Alaska Current (James Brooks, Alaska Beacon)
claims.notes: The article adds that 'those plans were not certain'. Keep that hedge.

claims.claim: AIDEA said it has not identified a specific project or projects for the Houston land.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA has not identified a specific project or projects for this land.
claims.source_outlet: The Alaska Current (James Brooks, Alaska Beacon)
claims.notes: Gives balance to any data center framing of the north end.

claims.claim: DNR reduced the conveyance to AIDEA from 19,500 acres to approximately 6,800 acres.
claims.verbatim: has determined that it is appropriate to reduce the conveyance acreage from 19,500 to approximately 6,800 acres.
claims.source_outlet: The Alaska Current (James Brooks, Alaska Beacon)
claims.notes: Quotes DNR's decision. DNR describes the purpose as 'a multi-use industrial and energy development district', not an 'industrial park'.

claims.claim: Terra Energy Center Corporation is a branch of Flatlands Energy, a subsidiary of Alberta-based Alaska Asia Clean Energy Corporation.
claims.verbatim: A branch of Flatlands Energy, itself a subsidiary of Alberta-based Alaska Asia Clean Energy Corporation,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Business (Rindi White)
claims.notes: Background from April 15th, outside the news window.

claims.claim: Terra Energy Center Corporation holds a land-use permit on about 1,000 acres near Lake Lorraine at Point MacKenzie.
claims.verbatim: TECC holds a land-use permit on about 1,000 acres near Lake Lorraine at Point MacKenzie,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Business (Rindi White)
claims.notes: Background as of April. The article says the permit is part of the borough's Port MacKenzie uplands. Its stated purpose is a feasibility study for 'an advanced manufacturing and computing campus'.

claims.claim: Alaska Business reported in April that Terra Energy Center Corporation isn't building a data center itself.
claims.verbatim: Although much of the Assembly’s discussion focused on data centers, TECC isn’t building a data center.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Business (Rindi White)
claims.notes: CONFLICT with how C13 might be read. This is why the Beacon's 'coal-fired computing data center' developer must stay unnamed. The plans may have changed since April.

claims.claim: By overriding a mayoral veto in March, the Mat-Su Borough Assembly authorized staff to work with a company pitching a coal-fired power plant near Skwentna to serve large consumers such as a data center.
claims.verbatim: By overriding a mayoral veto in March, the Matanuska-Susitna Borough Assembly authorized staff
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Business (Rindi White)
claims.notes: The sentence continues 'to work with a company pitching a new generation of coal-fired power plant near Skwentna' 'to provide electricity to Alaskans as well as large power consumers such as a data center.' It came back in three fragments of one sentence.

claims.claim: The Assembly let Terra Energy Center Corporation start a two-year joint international marketing effort with borough staff.
claims.verbatim: to embark on a two-year joint international marketing effort
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Business (Rindi White)
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy selected Terra Energy Center Corporation's planned 1,250 MW coal plant with carbon capture in the Mat-Su Borough for engineering and design funding.
claims.verbatim: 1,250 MW (target gross) nameplate-capacity
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of Energy
claims.notes: PRIMARY. The project title is 'Alaska Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage Coal Commissioning Project'. 1,250 MW is a target gross nameplate capacity, so say 'planned'. DOE says the developers target operation by 2031 (paraphrased by the tool, not verbatim). The Mat-Su siting and Anchorage base were paraphrased by the tool.

claims.claim: DOE's selection lists $89 million in federal funding for the Terra Energy Center project.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of Energy
claims.notes: The figure came back as a field value and not inside a sentence. This is a selection for negotiation, not an award paid out, so suggested wording is 'selected for up to $89 million' or 'selected for $89 million in DOE funding'. Page last updated October 5th.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins asked AIDEA to freeze plans for additional spending before he takes office on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: asked the agency to freeze any plans for additional spending before he takes office Dec. 7.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (James Brooks, Alaska Beacon)
claims.notes: This article doesn't mention Port MacKenzie or the rail match. The link between the pause and the rail match comes from the Beacon rail article (C16). The board adjourned at 3 p.m. Thursday, November 19th, without taking action.

claims.claim: The governor-elect's statement cited $200 million in AIDEA financial commitments since October.
claims.verbatim: $200 million in financial commitments since October.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (James Brooks, Alaska Beacon)
claims.notes: This is the governor-elect's characterization. Attribute it ('the governor-elect's office said').

claims.claim: NMFS published a proposed rule redefining pelagic trawl gear off Alaska in the Federal Register on November 16th.
claims.verbatim: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone off Alaska; Pelagic Trawl Gear Definition
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (National Marine Fisheries Service, NOAA)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. Vol. 91, No. 219, pages 73505 to 73513. The document title contains a semicolon, which is fine in a verbatim field. The text doesn't mention AI.

claims.claim: Comments on the pelagic trawl proposed rule are due by December 16th.
claims.verbatim: Submit comments on or before December 16, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (National Marine Fisheries Service, NOAA)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP.

claims.claim: The proposed rule would allow sensors and electronic instruments designed to adjust the gear, exclude bycatch or minimize contact with the seafloor.
claims.value: adjust the fishing gear, exclude bycatch, or minimize contact with the seafloor
claims.verbatim: (2) designed to adjust the fishing gear, exclude bycatch, or minimize contact with the seafloor.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (National Marine Fisheries Service, NOAA)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. This is the second of two categories. The first covers instruments that monitor the gear, catch or environment.

claims.claim: NMFS says live feed cameras that let operators see catch entering the net in real time have been widely adopted.
claims.verbatim: Live feed cameras have also been widely adopted that allow vessel operators to visualize catch entering the net in real time.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (National Marine Fisheries Service, NOAA)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP.

claims.claim: From 2019 to 2024, 147 vessels used pelagic trawl gear off Alaska.
claims.verbatim: From 2019 to 2024, 147 vessels utilized pelagic trawl gear.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register (National Marine Fisheries Service, NOAA)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP.
